# skilllib

The user manages agent skills with the `skilllib` CLI. Their **library** (`~/.skilllib/library`, "my skills", "the registry") holds versioned skills that load nowhere until added to a repo. Adding a skill pins it in the user's personal pins (`~/.skilllib/pins`, kept out of git: `personal: true`). `skilllib.json` is only for sharing a skill with the team, and only when they ask: `--shared` writes it, and they commit it.

Always pass `--json` (one line of JSON on stdout; messages go to stderr). A failure exits 1 with `{"error": "..."}` as that line. `link`, `tidy`, `global` (its listing, `keep` and `unkeep`), `restore`, `new`, `folders`, `harnesses`, `scan`, `search` (without `--json`) and `unhide` print messages only (read the exit code). Unknown flags are errors. Never run bare `skilllib` or `skilllib ui`: that's an interactive app.

## Reading

The **Now** section at the end has this repo's `status` and `list` output. Answer from it and don't run them again. If it shows the commands instead of their output, run both in parallel.

`status --json`: `skills` are this repo's own; `nested` (when there are any) are in subfolders such as monorepo packages, and load only when the agent works in their `dir`; `global` groups load in every repo, as this repo loads them (its `.claude/settings.json` can turn a plugin on or off); `issues` are everything skilllib finds wrong (out-of-date or missing skills, broken links, skills loaded twice), one `ids` entry per `problems` entry, with a `fix` (a safe repair; `skilllib doctor --fix` applies every fix, across all the user's projects), `choices` (decisions: propose one, and apply it once the user agrees, see Changing), or neither (reported only: tell the user what it says). When asked what's out of date or broken, `issues` and each skill's `state` are the answer. Don't audit skill contents unless asked.

- `source`: `library` (added with skilllib) · `repo` (the team's: committed to git, or in `.agents/skills` or `.grok/skills`) · `local` (only on this machine: not committed, not managed by skilllib) · `global` (a global folder an agent of yours reads: `~/.claude/skills`, `~/.agents/skills`, `~/.codex/skills`, `~/.cursor/skills`, `~/.grok/skills`) · `skills.sh` (`npx skills add`; `from` is the source repo) · `plugin` (Claude Code plugin; turn off with `/plugin`) · `claude.ai` (synced from the account) · `built-in` (bundled with an agent) · `system` (an admin's folder, such as `/etc/codex/skills`) · `skilllib` (this skill; `skilllib agent-skill remove` takes it out).
- Missing fields mean the usual: loaded by all of `agents`, state ok (or, for a repo's own or untracked skill, its usual state), in `.claude/skills`. `usesHere` counts Claude Code uses in this repo.

`list --json`: `inThisProject` (names) and `skills`, the library skills the repo doesn't have, each with a short `description` and the `projects` using it. To recommend, read the repo's README and manifests (see `files` in `status`) in one parallel step, then give a reason for each pick. Don't add a skill that already loads globally (it would load twice): offer to move it into just the repos that need it instead (`global move`). `show <name> --json` has the full SKILL.md.

Also: `usage --json` (Claude Code usage only, so "unused" is a hint; each skill lists the `projects` that used it), `projects --json` (every repo), `outdated --all --json`, `doctor --json` (every issue in every repo and globally, each with an `id`).

`check --json` reads the global skills and, in a repo, that repo's. It stores nothing. `brief` is the report: how many tokens the names and descriptions cost on every prompt, whether that is heavy, and the cuts that can actually be made. A Claude Code plugin it names turns off with `plugin off <id> --json`, and `plugin on <id>` puts it back. Run that only after the user agrees: the switch is global, and a skill in the plugin that was used goes too. Cursor plugins turn off in Cursor. claude.ai skills turn off on claude.ai. Built-ins ship with Cursor, Codex, and Grok, and skilllib can't unload them. Your own unused globals can move into the repos that need them. `uses` is Claude Code only, so 0 means it wasn't seen. Read `brief` to the user. The `skills` list is there if they ask about one.

## Changing (ask first unless the user asked for this exact change)

`plugin off|on <id>` (a Claude Code plugin, `name@marketplace` from `check`; a name alone works when only one plugin has it; it stays installed. The copy that loads in every repo. A per-repo install is left on, and the message says where) · `add <name>...` (personal pins; `--shared` writes `skilllib.json` for the team, and only when they asked to share it; `--personal` moves a shared pin back. Either flag moves an existing pin without changing its version. A pin stays where it already is) · `remove <name>...` (skills skilllib manages, `source: library`) · `update [name...]` · `sync` (installs what's pinned, personal pins and `skilllib.json`; takes no names). Pass several names in one call. Their result is `[{name, action, from, to, dirs, personal, moved, reason, blocked, uncommitted, inTheWay, backedUp}]` (`personal: true` when the pin is in your personal pins; `moved` when `--personal`/`--shared` moved it), which is the whole result: there's no need to check files afterwards. `import <dir>...` (into the library) prints `[{path, name, status}]` and exits 1 if a folder was skipped (`exists`, `no SKILL.md`). `doctor --fix` prints doctor's issues, each fix with `fixed: {ok, message}`.

- `skipped` + `reason`: nothing changed for that skill, and the command exits 1; tell the user. `--force` overwrites local edits (`backedUp` says where they went; `skilllib restore <name>` brings them back), but only use it with their OK.
- `removed` + `reason`: removed from skilllib.json, but something was left as it is (its copy behind a folder that links out of the repo, a file of the user's, or a link in such a folder). Tell the user what the reason says is still there.
- `action`: `installed`, `updated`, `reset` (edits overwritten), `relinked` (only links were written), `unchanged` (it was already there as asked), `removed`, `skipped`.
- `inTheWay`: something else is where a link goes (a file, or another copy), so that agent may not run this copy there, and the command exits 1. Tell the user what's there; once they move it, `skilllib link` adds the link. (A skills folder that's a file or links out of the repo makes the skill `skipped` instead, with the reason.)
- `blocked`: git tracks that folder. Re-run with `--allow-tracked` (for that command only) only with their OK.
- `uncommitted`: git tracks that folder but not the skill's real copy, so a link there would break for teammates; `--allow-tracked` doesn't change that. Once the copy is committed, `link --allow-tracked` adds it.
- Changes apply from the agent's next session. A `personal` change has nothing to commit. Without `personal` (`--shared`, or a pin that was already in `skilllib.json`), remind the user to commit `skilllib.json` and the folders in `dirs`.

**Prefer per-repo skills to global ones.** A global skill loads in every repo, for every agent. When `usage --json` shows one used in only a few repos, propose moving it there:

- `global move <name>... --to <repo>[,<repo>...]` (a project name from `projects`, or the path of a repo's top folder): imports it into the library, adds it to each repo, and only then stops loading it globally (restorable with `skilllib restore`). Prints `[{skill, moved, reason, left, projects: [{project, path, change}]}]` (`left`: links in a repo or its packages that now point at nothing, though a copy in the repo still serves them; tell the user to remove them); `moved: false` means it still loads globally, and `reason` says why.
- `global keep <name>...`: the user wants it everywhere; skilllib stops flagging it.

**Fixes and decisions.** `apply <id> [choice]` runs one problem's `fix`, or the choice you name: its label (safest), or its number from 1. With several choices it needs one. Prints `{id, applied, ok, message}`. Ids come from `issues` in `status --json` (Now, below) or from `doctor --json` (every repo; pass `apply` the same `--days` you gave `doctor`). A few issues span repos and offer different choices in each; then `apply` takes only the label.

**Importing and installing.** `import <dir>...` copies skill folders (each with a `SKILL.md`) into the library; it doesn't download anything. `install <source>...` does: `owner/repo`, `owner/repo@skill`, a `https://skills.sh/...` or GitHub URL, or a local folder. It puts each skill in the library. In a repo it also adds them here; `--global` loads them in every repo instead (and marks them kept). A repo with several skills is listed, not installed, until you pass `@name` or `--all`. `search <query>` lists matches from skills.sh. `install` and `search` accept `--json`.

## Now

This repo (`skilllib status --json`):
!`skilllib status --json`

Library skills it could add (`skilllib list --json`):
!`skilllib list --json`

# ◆ skilllib **Manage your agent skills like dependencies, or let your agents do it.**
One library for all your skills. Each repo gets only the ones it needs,
and every agent you use can see them. [![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/skilllib?color=8b9dff&label=npm)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/skilllib) [![license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-6bcb77)](LICENSE) ![node](https://img.shields.io/badge/node-%E2%89%A522-5eb8f7) ![agents](https://img.shields.io/badge/works%20with-Claude%20Code%20%C2%B7%20Cursor%20%C2%B7%20Codex%20%C2%B7%20Copilot%20%C2%B7%20Gemini%20%C2%B7%20OpenCode%20%C2%B7%20Zed%20%C2%B7%20Grok%20%C2%B7%20and%20more-c792ea) ```bash npm install -g skilllib && skilllib agent-skill install ``` Then ask your agent: *"Which skills can you use here, and which of my global skills should only load in this repo?"*
--- ## The problem [Agent skills](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills) (folders with a `SKILL.md`) are one of the best ways to teach Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Zed and Grok how *you* work. But they pile up quickly: - **`npx skills add`** drops skills into `~/.agents/skills`. - **Plugins** bring their own. - **claude.ai** syncs a few more. - **Your teammates** commit some to the repo. - **You** copy folders into `~/.claude/skills` "just for now". A few weeks later: - **🌍 Global skills load everywhere.** Everything in `~/.claude/skills` or `~/.agents/skills` loads in **every repo, in every session**. Your agent reads the name and description of your Stripe skill while fixing Terraform in your infra repo. That costs context, and skills fire when they shouldn't. - **👯 Duplicates.** The same skill arrives through `npx skills` *and* a plugin *and* a copy in the repo, and your agent sees it twice. - **🙈 Each agent looks somewhere else.** Claude Code reads `.claude/skills`; Codex and Zed read `.agents/skills`; Cursor reads both. Grok reads `.grok/skills` and `.agents/skills`, and by default the Claude and Cursor folders too. The skills your team committed to `.agents/skills` are invisible to Claude Code. - **🧟 Copies drift.** You improved a skill in one repo; the other five still have the old version. - **🤷 No overview.** Which skills does this repo actually have? Where did each one come from? Is it committed, or only on my laptop? Does anyone use it? Most agents can't turn off a global skill for just one repo. Claude Code can, but Cursor and Codex can't. **The only real fix is to stop using global skills and give each repo what it needs.** ## How skilllib fixes it - **🤖 Your agents run it.** One small skill teaches Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Zed and Grok to use the skilllib CLI. Ask them what's loaded here, what to add, what's out of date, or to move a global skill into the repos that use it. The commands agents use have `--json` output shaped for them, and they ask before changing anything. - **📚 Your skills: one versioned library.** Every skill has a single master copy in `~/.skilllib/library`, and each change becomes a new version. - **📦 Per-repo installs, pinned like dependencies.** Each repo lists its skills and versions in `skilllib.json`. `sync` reproduces them exactly, and `update` moves to the newest. - **🤝 One copy, every agent.** skilllib puts one real copy in the repo and links it into whichever folders your other agents read. - **🧹 Health: one list of what to fix.** Global skills you haven't decided about, skills loaded twice, duplicate copies, updates, broken links, each with its fix. For a global skill: move it to the repos that need it, keep it global, or delete it. Usage numbers and descriptions help you, or your agent, decide. - **✓ Global on purpose.** Some skills belong everywhere. Mark them once and skilllib stops warning about them. - **🔎 See everything in a repo:** - where each skill comes from (the repo, your library, global, a plugin, claude.ai…) - which agents load it - whether it's committed to git or gitignored - how often it was used - **🖥 An app when you want to look yourself.** `skilllib` opens a terminal app with the same data and fixes, and can copy a review prompt for any agent. - **🛟 Nothing is lost.** Your library keeps the skills you remove from a repo, and everything else skilllib removes goes to a backup you can restore with one key. Everything runs locally: no server and no account. `skilllib install` and `skilllib search` are the exception: they talk to [skills.sh](https://skills.sh) and GitHub to fetch a skill. --- ## Quick start It needs **Node.js 22+** and works on macOS and Linux. Windows support is newer: it uses directory junctions, so no admin rights are needed. ### With your agents ```bash npm install -g skilllib skilllib agent-skill install skilllib install anthropics/skills@frontend-design ``` `skilllib agent-skill install` puts the `skilllib` skill where your agents look, in every repo (see [Use it from your agents](#use-it-from-your-agents)). Start a new agent session in any repo and ask away. `skilllib install` puts a skill in your library and, when you run it inside a repo, adds it there so every agent you use can see it. `skilllib search react` finds skills on [skills.sh](https://skills.sh). To load one in every repo, add `--global`. ### In the app ```bash skilllib # or: npx skilllib ``` On first run, skilllib asks two things: 1. **Which agents you use.** The ones installed on your machine are pre-selected. `skilllib harnesses` lists every one skilllib knows. 2. **Where your projects live**, e.g. `~/Projects`. It finds every git repo in there, and rescans each time it opens. Agent worktrees (`/.claude/worktrees/*`) aren't counted as projects. Then a good first session looks like this: 1. **You land in Places, on the repo you're in.** `enter` opens its skills; `enter` again opens a skill's issues and actions. 2. **Open Health** to see everything worth fixing, in every repo and in your global skills: what `skilllib doctor` reports. **✦ Fix N issues automatically…** does the safe ones; the rest are your call, one at a time. 3. **Add skills** to a repo with **+ Add a skill…**, the top row of its list. --- ## Use it from your agents `skilllib agent-skill install` puts a small `skilllib` skill in the global skill folders your agents read: one real copy (usually `~/.claude/skills` or `~/.agents/skills`) and a link in each of the others. This is the one skill that should be global, because it's about every repo. Upgrading skilllib keeps it up to date, and `skilllib agent-skill remove` takes it out. Agents use it from their next session. Then ask in plain words. A few examples, with what the agent runs: | Ask | The agent runs | |---|---| | *Which skills can you use here, and where does each come from?* | `status --json`, which Claude Code gets as the skill loads, so it answers in one step | | *Which of my skills should this repo use?* | `list --json`, then reads the README and manifests, and gives a reason for each pick | | *Which skills do I use most? Which ones never?* | `usage --json` (Claude Code usage only, so "never" is a hint) | | *Move my global skills into the repos that actually use them.* | `usage --json` to see where each is used, then `global move --to `, or `global keep ` for the ones you want everywhere | | *Is anything broken or out of date? Fix it.* | `status --json` or `doctor --json`, then `doctor --fix` for the safe repairs and `apply ` for each decision you approve | | *Add the skill from github.com/acme/skills to my library.* | Clones the repo into a temporary folder, then `import ` and `add `. skilllib itself downloads nothing | The agent asks before it changes anything, unless you asked for that exact change. Anything skilllib removes can be restored: see [Backups](#backups). --- ## The app ### The screen Three panes: **Places** on the left, a **list** on the right, and the **details** of what you select under it. Terminals under 80 columns get a tab bar instead of Places; under 30 rows, details open on `enter`. | Place | What it shows | |---|---| | **Your skills** | Your library: master copies, versioned. Nothing here loads anywhere until you add it to a repo. | | **Global** | Everything your agents load in *every* repo: yours, plus vendor skills (plugins, claude.ai, Cursor built-ins). | | **Plugins** | Every plugin installed, on or off: what it brings, where it's installed, and how much its skills get used. Turn it on or off, update it, uninstall it, or replace it with library skills. | | **Health** | What `skilllib doctor` reports, in every repo and in Global, each with its fix or choices. | | **Projects** | Every repo found in your project folders. `◆` marks the one you're in; `✕` `⚠` its worst issue. | | **Settings** | Your agents and the skilllib skill for them, your project folders, hidden repos, and backups. | | **Help** | The keys and symbols. | ### Keys | Key | Does | |---|---| | *type* | Filter the pane you're in. Word initials work too: `cfw` finds `cloudflare-workers`. | | `↑` `↓` | Move | | `enter` `→` | One pane deeper: Places → list → details. In the details, apply the selected fix or action. | | `esc` `←` | One pane back (`esc` clears a filter first). In the details, `←` `→` move along a line of actions and `↑` `↓` between lines. | | `space` | Apply the ★ recommended fix, or show the choices when it's your call; on a group, open or close it | | `tab` | Next tab: All · Issues · Local · Global · Plugins · Vendor | | `ctrl+r` | Read everything again from disk · `ctrl+c` quits | ### A repo The list shows everything agents can use in the repo, one row per skill, even when it loads from several places: | Column | Meaning | |---|---| | Source | `lib v2`: from your library · `repo`: the team's (committed to git, or in `.agents/skills` or `.grok/skills`) · `untracked`: only on this machine · `global` (`global ✓`: global on purpose) · `⧉ plugin` · `claude.ai` · `cursor` · `grok` | | Uses | Claude Code uses in this repo, last 30 days | | Issue | The worst of its issues; the details show them all | **Related skills fold into one row**, here, in Global and in Your skills. skilllib groups them by the strongest signal it has: the same source (a plugin, an `npx skills` repo, claude.ai, Cursor), then folders you copied in the same minute (a whole set installed at once), then the same first word (`cloudflare-*`). `→` opens a group and `←` closes it; `enter` on an open group shows actions for all of it: move all to repos, keep all global, delete all, add all to repos, or a review prompt. A group you move together is recorded as its skills' origin, so it stays grouped in your library. The top rows start something: **+ Add a skill…**, **✦ Fix N issues automatically…**, and **⋯ repo…** (open its folder, hide it from the list, copy a review prompt for its skills). A skill's details show each issue with its fixes (★ is the recommended one; *your call* marks decisions, which are never applied automatically), then its other actions, how often it's used here, and where it loads from with its git state. What skilllib flags: | Issue | Fixes | |---|---| | **Repo and global copies** (a repo copy of a skill that also loads globally) | Stop loading it globally. Your call: that changes every repo, so it's offered only when no repo of yours that has or pins the skill would be left with only the global copy for an agent (otherwise the issue says who, and what to do first), and when the global copy is a version in Your skills. If you keep it global on purpose, remove the repo copies skilllib installed instead | | **Also in a plugin** | Remove the plugin or turn it off, or turn it off in this repo only (`.claude/settings.local.json`, a local-only file git ignores), or remove your copy from this repo. Cursor ignores repo settings, so once the repo turns the plugin off, only turning the plugin off or removing it helps there | | **Folder missing** · **No longer in your library** | Sync the project · copy it back into your library | | **Not the pinned version** (the copy is another version from your library, e.g. after a pull) | Install the pinned versions (`sync`; a choice when the copies are committed) | | **Out of date** · **Edited here** | Update every out-of-date skill in the repo (or one, from its *Update to vN* action) · save the edits as a new version, or discard them | | **Not every agent can use it** | Add the links (links only; nothing is copied or moved). If git tracks a folder a link would go in, you choose whether git sees it | | **Differs from your library** · **Not tracked** · **Not in your library** · **From npx skills** | Update your library from it, or replace it with your library's (the team's committed copy is only copied) · track it · import it · import it | | **Unused 30 days** | Remove the ones skilllib installed from the repo | | **Broken link** (in a repo) | Remove it (your call when git tracks the link). Next to a real copy it's tidy's: it points it at the copy where an agent needs that folder, and removes it otherwise | | **Pinned version not in your library** | Install your newest (the folder is missing and your library has no copy of what skilllib.json pins) | | **Broken link** · **Not reviewed** (global) | Remove the link · move it to repos, keep it global on purpose, or delete it (the row's actions) | | **Not every agent can use it** (global) | Link it into that agent's global folder, e.g. a Codex skill in `~/.agents/skills` or `~/.codex/skills` gets a link in `~/.claude/skills` | These are the issues `skilllib doctor` reports, with the same fixes and choices. ### Adding and removing skills - **+ Add a skill…** searches your library. Tick several with `space` and add them in one go; a plugin's skills (e.g. ponytail and its `ponytail-*` commands) sit under one row that ticks or adds them all. Its last rows create a new skill (it opens in `$EDITOR`, and goes into the repo when you close it) or copy a prompt for an agent to write it. - **Adding** copies the newest version into the fewest folders your agents read, and pins it (see [Personal or shared pins](#personal-or-shared-pins)). Agents pick it up in their next session. The layout matches `npx skills`' symlink option: the real copy lives in `.agents/skills`, which nearly every agent reads, and Claude Code gets a link. Grok reads `.agents/skills` and, by default, `.claude/skills`, so it never needs its own copy. - Claude Code, with or without Cursor or Grok: `.claude/skills/`. - Cursor, Codex, Zed or Grok without Claude Code: `.agents/skills/`. - Claude Code plus Codex or Zed: the copy goes in `.agents/skills`, with a link in `.claude/skills`. Claude Code only reads `.claude/skills`, and Codex and Zed don't read it. - **Remove from repo** deletes that copy and its links; your library keeps it. When the copy itself sits where skilllib doesn't write (a skills folder that links out of the repo, or a file where the copy goes), it drops just the pin and leaves that copy as it is; a link in such a folder is left too, and said. In the app, an untracked copy goes to Settings › Backups instead (`skilllib remove` only removes skills skilllib manages). If you edited a tracked skill here, skilllib asks first, and the edits go to Settings › Backups. - **The repo's own skills are never deleted by skilllib.** You can copy them into your library, or link them so every agent sees them. - **Git-tracked folders:** if the repo commits the folder a link would go into (common for `.agents/skills`), the app asks once and remembers your yes for that repo (in `~/.skilllib/config.json`, `allowTracked`); on the command line, `--allow-tracked` allows it for that one command (doctor's *Add links everywhere* choice remembers it, as the app does). If you say no, it tells you which agents can't see the skill there. A skill whose copy git doesn't share (not committed, and not in a folder the repo commits) never gets a link in a committed folder: teammates would get a broken link. ### …[文件过长——仅保留首 16KB 与末 8KB]… r; outside a repo, `status --json` lists only the global skills. Flags: `--personal` / `--shared` (for `add`: pin in your personal pins or in the repo's `skilllib.json`; see [Personal or shared pins](#personal-or-shared-pins)), `--force` (overwrite local edits, backed up to `~/.skilllib/edit-backup`), `--allow-tracked` (link into git-tracked folders, for that command only; skills git doesn't share are still left out), `--days N`, `--json`. For `tidy`: `--dry-run` (preview), `--allow-git` (also change committed files), ` --keep ` (the copy that wins when copies differ). A command exits 1 when it couldn't do all you asked: a skill skipped (not in the library, or local edits in the way), links git-tracked folders blocked, a link something else is in the way of (a file or another copy), an unknown `tidy` name or `--keep` folder, or (with `--all`, and `projects`) a repo left out because its `skilllib.json` can't be read. What it did do is still done, and listed. An unknown or misspelled flag is an error too, so a typo never runs silently. With `--json`, an error that stops a command prints `{"error": "…"}` on stdout as well as the message on stderr. The commands SKILL.md lists as messages-only print nothing on stdout otherwise: read their exit code. **`--json`** prints one line of JSON on stdout, for scripts and agents. Messages and warnings go to stderr. It works with `status`, `list`, `show`, `projects`, `outdated`, `usage`, `doctor`, `apply`, `add`, `remove`, `sync`, `update`, `import`, `global move`, `agent-skill`, `check` and `plugin`. The output is shaped to keep agents fast and cheap: - **`status --json`** answers everything about the repo in one call: - the repo's skills, with their source, version, state and git state - skills in subfolders (`nested`, e.g. monorepo packages), with their folder - the global skills, grouped by where they come from, with the plugins the repo's `.claude/settings.json` turns on or off - every problem skilllib found here, with its fix or choices and an id for `skilllib apply` - how often Claude Code used each skill here - the repo's top-level files Skills that share every attribute are grouped, and attributes at their usual value are left out. - **`list --json`**: inside a repo, the library skills the repo already has (names only), and the others with a short description (its first sentence, or the start of it). - **`add`, `remove`, `sync` and `update`** list each change, and (except `remove`) the folders it wrote to, so there's nothing left to check. The `skilllib` skill runs `status` and `list` as it loads (in Claude Code), so an agent usually answers "which skills can you use here?" in one step. **TypeScript types.** The package ships a type for each command's JSON (`StatusJson`, `ListJson`, `ChangesJson`, `DoctorJson`…). It has types only, no runtime API: ```ts import { execFileSync } from "node:child_process"; import type { StatusJson } from "skilllib"; const status: StatusJson = JSON.parse(execFileSync("skilllib", ["status", "--json"], { encoding: "utf-8" })); ``` A field is only removed or changed in a major version. ## Files | Path | What | |---|---| | `/skilllib.json` | Skills you shared with the team (`--shared`). **Commit it** with the skill folders. Absent until then | | `~/.skilllib/pins/` | Your personal pins, one file per repo (by its remote). Keep it in git with your library to use them on other machines. | | `~/.skilllib/library/` | Your skills (master copies). Worth putting under git. | | `~/.skilllib/store/` | Every version of every skill, immutable | | `~/.skilllib/config.json` | Your agents, project folders, hidden projects, skills you keep global | | `~/.skilllib/projects.json` | Repos skilllib has seen. Rewritten only when that list changes | | `~/.skilllib/usage-cache.json` | Parsed Claude Code transcripts, so the next `status` doesn't read them again. Safe to delete | | `~/.skilllib/trash/`, `global-backup/`, `tidy-backup/`, `edit-backup/` | Everything skilllib removed, restorable from Settings › Backups | | `~/.skilllib/plugin-backup.json` | Plugins skilllib uninstalled (with their scope and repo), so Settings › Backups can reinstall them | | `~/.skilllib/review-prompt.md` | The last review prompt you copied | | `~/.claude/skills/skilllib/` | The skill that lets your agents use skilllib (`agent-skill install`) | Environment variables: `SKILLLIB_HOME` moves `~/.skilllib`, `$VISUAL` / `$EDITOR` set the editor, `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` is honored for Claude Code, `CODEX_HOME` for Codex, and `GROK_HOME` for Grok. Grok does not honor `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`. ## FAQ **Does it change my repos?** Only when you tell it to: adding, removing, linking or tidying a skill. That updates your `~/.skilllib/pins/` and the repo's `.git/info/exclude`, or `skilllib.json` when you share a skill with the team. It asks before linking a shared skill into a folder git tracks, and before tidy changes a committed file. It never deletes the only copy of a repo's own skill. **Can I share skills with my team?** Commit `skilllib.json` along with the skill folders (`.agents/skills`, and `.claude/skills` if you use Claude Code). Or keep `~/.skilllib/library` in a git repo of its own (the rest of `~/.skilllib` is personal: config, backups, the version store), and run `skilllib import` on teammates' machines from a clone of it. **Do I have to commit `skilllib.json`?** Only for a skill you shared with the team (`skilllib add --shared`). Everything else stays in your personal pins, out of git. See [Personal or shared pins](#personal-or-shared-pins). **Why does usage only count Claude Code?** It's the only agent whose transcripts skilllib reads. Grok keeps sessions under `~/.grok/sessions`, and Cursor doesn't keep them locally. Codex's format hasn't been tested yet. That's why "unused" is a strong hint, not proof. **What's not supported yet?** - Grok plugins: they stay off until named in `~/.grok/config.toml`, and skilllib doesn't read that list yet. - Turning off Cursor marketplace plugins: skilllib lists them and reports ones that duplicate your skills, but Cursor doesn't record which plugins are on in a file skilllib can read. - Installing plugins from a marketplace: use `/plugin` in Claude Code. Plugins a repo's own `.claude/settings.json` turns on without installing them aren't listed in Plugins yet. - Unloading a `npx skills` skill doesn't update that tool's lock file. - Downloading skills: `skilllib install owner/repo`, `owner/repo@skill`, a skills.sh or GitHub URL, or a local folder. It imports into your library and, in a repo, adds the skill here. `--global` loads it in every repo. `skilllib search ` looks up skills.sh. A repo with many skills is listed until you name one or pass `--all`. Everything else skilllib does stays on this machine. --- ## Development ```bash pnpm install pnpm test && pnpm type-check && pnpm build # tests run on bun pnpm dev # run from source pnpm design # render the TUI screens in docs/design npm link # use your checkout as `skilllib` ``` How the TUI is designed, and why: [docs/DESIGN.md](docs/DESIGN.md). **Releasing:** automatic, with [release-please](https://github.com/googleapis/release-please). Don't edit `version` by hand. 1. Write commits (and PR titles) as [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/): `fix:` → patch, `feat:` → minor, `feat!:` or a `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer → major. `docs:`, `ci:`, `chore:`, `test:` and `refactor:` don't release. 2. After each merge to `main`, release-please keeps one PR, **chore(main): release X.Y.Z**, up to date with the next version and its `CHANGELOG.md`. 3. Merge that PR when you want to release. It tags `vX.Y.Z` and creates the GitHub release; CI then tests, builds and publishes to npm through [trusted publishing](https://docs.npmjs.com/trusted-publishers) (no token; provenance is automatic). The earlier registry-server version (Next.js, Postgres, S3) lives on the `archive/registry-server` branch. ## License [MIT](LICENSE) © Toni Tralice
